passages.provision_quote: This section may only be enforced prospectively. This section does not apply retroactively and shall not be construed to apply to the conduct of any person who entered this state unlawfully from a foreign nation at any time before this section becomes enforceable.
passages.note: The new illegal-entry crime and its return-to-home-country order apply only to future entries, expressly exempting anyone who entered before the section becomes enforceable.
Senate Third Reading roll call shows Shope voting Y on HCR2060.
Bill history page confirms the Senate Third Reading of HCR2060 passed on 2024-05-22.

rows.reasoning: Shope voted Y on Senate Third Reading of HCR2060 (2024), the Secure the Border Act, whose new illegal-entry-and-return-order article states it 'does not apply retroactively and shall not be construed to apply to the conduct of any person who entered this state unlawfully from a foreign nation at any time before this section becomes enforceable,' so only future illegal entrants are subject to prosecution and a court-ordered return to their home country while everyone who already entered is left alone. That matches rung 3, 'Focus deportation on recent arrivals while leaving long-settled undocumented immigrants in place,' and the bill's own text excludes rungs 1 (it creates a removal mechanism), 2 (the predicate offense is illegal entry, not a serious violent crime), 4 and 5 (both require ultimately reaching the existing, long-settled population, which this section permanently exempts).
